scope: Kubernetes v1.36.1 on disposable local kind clusters. Compare the stock kube-controller-manager with a profile that sets the legacy controller exclusion flag. Observe that no legacy token Secret is auto-generated and both profiles still populate an explicitly requested fixture. Apply namespace-scoped admission and confirm it rejects the same request while a harmless Pod still receives a projected, expiring bound token. Only boolean field-presence and boolean JWT-claim observations are retained; no token or Secret data is emitted. This does not assess production or managed-provider configuration.

checks.claim: Stock kubeadm controller-manager has the legacy token controller enabled
The ServiceAccount has no auto-generated long-lived token Secret reference
With the stock controller, an explicitly requested legacy Secret is populated
Projected token is present, time bounded, audience-bearing, and bound to Pod and ServiceAccount claims
The live kube-controller-manager process has the controller exclusion flag
The ServiceAccount has no auto-generated long-lived token Secret reference
With the exclusion flag present, an explicitly requested legacy Secret is populated
Admission rejects the identical explicit legacy Secret create
